text: In 1943, America built a bomb made of bats.
It started with a dentist named Lytle Adams, who visited a cave in New Mexico full of bats.
His idea: strap a tiny firebomb to every bat, and drop them over Japan, where many houses were made of wood and paper.
The bats would hide in the attics.
Then the timers would go off.
The man who invented napalm designed bombs small enough for a bat to carry.
Then, during a test in New Mexico, some armed bats escaped.
And they did exactly what they were designed to do.
They found the nearest dark hiding place.
Luckily, the bat bomb worked perfectly.
Unluckily, it worked on the army's own air base.
The fire burned down the test range, and even the general's car.
After two million dollars, the project was cancelled.
The bats never fought in the war.
But they did win one battle.
